properties.citation: Traced by EthniAfrica (20 October 2026) after Spiridon Ion Cepleanu, « Groupes ethniques de Côte d'Ivoire », Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:IvoryCoastEthno.jpg, itself after P. Vennetier, Atlas de la Côte d'Ivoire, Éditions du Jaguar, 1978, map 34b; checked against G. P. Murdock, Tribal Map of Africa (1959), digitised by Nathan Nunn. The polygon of the Baoulé.
properties.derivation: Built by social/video/areas.mjs: the research's polygon yk-baoule.geojson, kept inside the Natural Earth 1:50m polygon of Côte d'Ivoire (ADM0_A3 CIV) so its outer edge is the country's; on a 0.05° grid (cells whose centre falls inside), traced back as the cell boundary, simplified by Douglas–Peucker at 0.05° and rounded to 0.01°; parts and holes under 5000 km² dropped. The Baoulé have since settled far beyond this area (west-central cocoa belt, Abidjan); the area shows where the sources place the people, not where Baoulé people live today.
